    "rationale": "What the evidence shows: the race data (60 trials, 0 finishes) is for the iteration-0 design (kp 6.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.5, 0.016 m sensors at 0.012 m spacing). Every run ended off track. Max error reached 0.064 m, above the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stayed at 0.025 to 0.030. So the failures are peak excursions, not a steady drift. Line losses averaged 1.0 to 2.0 per run, and steering oscillation was 0.14 to 0.19.\n\nWhat I kept: base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'last_direction', and the 0.016 m sensor footprint. Speed is kept because completion is worth 500 points and needs about 1.5 m/s, and the race did not show that speed itself caused the failures. The 0.016 m footprint is kept because its overlap is what the critique asked for.\n\nWhat I changed and why:\n(1) Geometry: 7 sensors at 0.012 m spacing (x from -0.036 to +0.036) instead of 5. A tape edge is visible to a sensor while the tape centre is within about 0.045 m of the sensor, so the old outer sensor at 0.024 m lost the line near 0.045 m. This was the likely cause of line losses on the wide excursions. The outer sensors now reach about 0.056 m, close to the 0.06 m limit, so the robot keeps a readable signal while the error is still recoverable. Weights are spread evenly, [-1, -0.67, -0.33, 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1], so |signal| stays at most 1.\n(2) kp 6.0 to 5.0. This is a partial change. The critique is right that kp 4.0 gives less authority at the peaks, where the failures happen, so I did not cut it hard. I also do not accept the claim that kp 6 caused overshoot: the data does not show it. The 5.0 value is a modest step to reduce jitter while keeping most of the corrective force at peaks.\n(3) ki 0.3 to 0.1. The critique is right that ki 0.3 was large relative to the signal (the integral is capped at plus or minus 2, so it gives up to 0.6 turn). With the integral capped, 0.1 is enough to trim a steady offset without windup risk on the peaks.\n(4) kd 0.5 to 0.2. I accept the critique that a derivative term on a quantised, noisy 100 Hz signal amplifies jitter, so kd should stay small. I do not drop it to zero, because some damping of fast signal changes is still useful.\n\nRejected: the critique's suggestion to cut base_speed sharply, because completion depends on speed. Rejected also: the claim that the current sensor array has no overlap, which is only true for the draft's 0.02 m spacing and not for the raced design.\n\nExpected result: max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, line_loss_events under 1.0 per run, steering_oscillation below 0.15, and at least some completions on the oval.\n\nHypotheses and next rules: if line_loss_events stay above 1.5, the problem is at the outer edges, so lower base_speed by 0.1. If max_error stays above 0.06 with low oscillation, raise kp by 0.5. If oscillation is above 0.2, lower kp by 0.5 before changing kd. If completion_time exceeds 3 s on a run that finishes, raise base_speed by 0.1. If rms_error shows a steady offset, raise ki in steps of 0.05. Robustness to the unseen track is argued from the wider sensor array and the moderate gains, not tuned to the development shapes.",
